sections.h2: Where are Hays County property records kept?
sections.html:
The Hays County Clerk's Records Division keeps the county's official public records, which run from 1848 to the present and include deeds, deeds of trust and liens. You can view and buy copies through the clerk's online Self-Service portal or on the computers in the office lobby, and archived record books can be read in the office. For questions about official public records, the Records Division lists the address recordsdivision@hayscountytx.gov.

The clerk's office has three divisions: Records, Courts and Commissioners Court. Probate and guardianship support sits with the Courts Division, which matters when the owner of a house has died. Divorce and family court files are held by the District Clerk, so a title question that involves a divorce decree may need a stop at that office too.

San Marcos is the main site, and the clerk also runs three substations. Each substation keeps weekday hours of 8 am to 4:30 pm and closes for lunch from noon to 1 pm:

  • Precinct 2, Kyle: 5458 FM 2770, Suite 120, phone 512-878-6687
  • Precinct 3, Wimberley: 200 Stillwater, Suite 101, phone 512-878-6684
  • Precinct 4, Dripping Springs: 195 Roger Hanks Pkwy, Suite 113, phone 512-878-6683

Call before you drive to a substation and confirm it takes the filing you have in hand.

sections.h2: How do I search Hays County land records online?
sections.html:
Use the clerk's Self-Service portal, which opens on a disclaimer you must accept before searching. The disclaimer says the clerk does not certify the information shown, that the index works like a library card catalogue, and that you should try every spelling variation of a name. Use the index to find the recorded document, then read the document itself.

When you check a Hays County house before a sale, these searches catch most surprises:

  • Every owner name on the chain of title, with and without middle initials, suffixes and former surnames.
  • Each deed of trust, then a matching release. A loan paid off years ago can still show as open if the release was never filed.
  • Judgments, abstracts and state tax liens. The state clerk manual says the Comptroller files state tax lien notices with the county clerk, who records them in a state tax lien book.
  • Notices of foreclosure sale, which the clerk posts and files.

The clerk also offers Fraud Guard, a free alert: sign up and you get an email whenever a document with your name gets recorded. It is a cheap early warning against a forged deed on a rental house or vacant lot.

sections.h2: What makes a deed recordable in Hays County?
sections.html:
Texas lets the clerk record a deed only after the signer acknowledges it to a notary or other authorized officer, or swears to it in front of two subscribing witnesses (Property Code 12.001(b)). Filing follows the land, so a house in Kyle, Wimberley or Dripping Springs is recorded with the Hays County Clerk.

The state clerk manual names the usual instruments in the deed records: general and special warranty deeds, quitclaim deeds, trustee's deeds, sheriff's deeds, tax deeds, affidavits, releases of deeds of trust, leases, contracts of sale and powers of attorney. It also sets the fee building blocks. The first page is $5.00 and each added page is $4.00, with several smaller county fees for records management, archives and technology on top. A missing grantee mailing address can add $25. Get the current total from the Hays clerk before you mail anything.

The same manual notes that commissioners courts may direct clerks to waive real property recording fees for buyers who use certain federal or state grant programs. If a buyer in your sale is using one, ask whether Hays County has adopted that waiver.

sections.h2: Who sets value and bills tax in Hays County?
sections.html:
Two offices handle the money side, and neither is the clerk. The Hays Central Appraisal District in Kyle sets value, runs the property search, and processes exemptions, while the Hays County Tax Office sends bills and takes payments. The district's own site says it neither mails tax bills nor processes payments.

The district lists its office at 21001 North IH 35 in Kyle, phone (512) 268-2522, with weekday hours from 8 to 5 and a drop box at the front door. Its online forms cover a homestead exemption, an agricultural use application, a business personal property rendition and a change of address. Bills and payment instructions are on the county tax office site at tax.co.hays.tx.us.

Hays CAD also audits every granted homestead once every five years under Tax Code 11.43(h-1). An owner who gets an audit letter should answer it with a copy of a valid Texas driver's license or state ID whose address matches the house. If the letter is ignored, the exemption gets a termination date. Appraisal day for the whole state is January 1, homestead notices start around April 1, and the usual protest deadline is mid-May.

sections.h2: Which record problems slow a Hays County house sale?
sections.html:
Old liens, unpaid tax and missing heirs top the list. Each January 1 a Texas tax lien attaches to secure that year's bill, so an unpaid balance travels with the house through a sale. Tax still open after January 31 turns delinquent on February 1 with a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest.

Inherited houses add their own steps:

  • A transfer on death deed has to be on record before the owner's death.
  • A muniment of title order and the will go on file with the clerk.
  • An affidavit of heirship is a sworn statement placed on file with the clerk, and nothing in the law makes a buyer or title company take it.
  • Heirs who are not named on a recorded deed need to give the appraisal district an affidavit of ownership interest, the death certificate and a recent utility bill before they can get the homestead exemption.

A notice of foreclosure sale is also filed with the clerk, at least 21 days ahead of the first-Tuesday auction. A notice on file against a Hays County house means the sale clock is already running.

faqs.q: Which office records a deed in Hays County?
faqs.a: The Records Division of the Hays County Clerk handles it, and the division's files reach back to 1848. A Hays County house is filed with the Hays County Clerk.

faqs.q: Can I search Hays County deeds online?
faqs.a: Yes, through the clerk's Self-Service portal, where records can be viewed and purchased. The portal asks you to accept a disclaimer first, and it advises trying every spelling of a name.

faqs.q: Does the appraisal district record my deed?
faqs.a: No. The appraisal district sets value and handles exemptions from Kyle, and the clerk is the one who records the deed. Owners usually update the district separately, for example by using its online change of address form.

faqs.q: Who sends the Hays County property tax bill?
faqs.a: The Hays County Tax Office mails the bills and accepts payment. Call it, and skip the appraisal district, for any question about an amount owed.

faqs.q: What happens if a deed has no grantee mailing address?
faqs.a: The clerk may add a $25 charge. Put a mailing address for every buyer on the deed before you file.
